name: Familial Hypofibrinogenemia

criteria.description: Persistently reduced plasma fibrinogen levels below normal reference range
Positive family history of hypofibrinogenemia or bleeding diathesis
Identification of pathogenic mutations in fibrinogen genes (FGA, FGB, or FGG)
Clinical evidence of bleeding tendency such as mucocutaneous bleeding or prolonged bleeding after trauma

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low plasma fibrinogen levels plus either a positive family history or pathogenic fibrinogen gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of acquired causes of hypofibrinogenemia.

laboratory: Reduced plasma fibrinogen concentration (functional and antigenic assays)
Prolonged thrombin time and reptilase time
imaging: Imaging may reveal hemorrhagic complications such as intracranial bleeding or hemarthrosis
other: Family pedigree consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of fibrinogen rather than reduced levels
Secondary to liver disease, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or massive transfusion
No family history or genetic mutations
Normal or near-normal fibrinogen antigen levels with dysfunctional fibrinogen

references: Federici AB. Congenital fibrinogen disorders: an update. Semin Thromb Hemost. 2018;44(4):333-339.
Casini A, et al. Diagnosis and management of congenital fibrinogen disorders. Haematologica. 2015;100(7):891-896.
